proposals.before: His son Huo Yi, styled Shaoxian, ended the Former Ruler’s reign as a gentleman attendant at the heir’s residence.
proposals.after: His son Huo Yi, styled Shaoxian, in the last years of the Former Ruler’s reign became a gentleman attendant at the heir’s residence.
proposals.reason: Chinese 先主末年為 means in the last years of the Former Sovereign he became X, not that he ended the reign.

proposals.before: Chong's younger brother Xiang Chong served as colonel of the army of loud-shouting archers and as master of writing.
proposals.after: Chong's younger brother Xiang Chong (名充) served as colonel of the army of loud-shouting archers and as master of writing.
proposals.reason: Chinese distinguishes 寵 and 充; English uses Xiang Chong for both without marking 充.

decisions.reason: 先主末年 means 'in the last years of the Former Ruler's reign'; the current English incorrectly makes Huo Yi end the reign.

向寵 and his younger brother 向充 are distinct people whose names are both conventionally romanized Xiang Chong. Inserting a bare Chinese-character parenthesis into the prose is not an English translation improvement; their structured people records already preserve the distinction.
